where: Section 3 (paragraph on the trade-off) and Exam traps, third bullet
problem: The switching count is wrong by a factor of two. The text says "Each pulse edge is a commutation, so p pulses per half cycle give 2p commutations per cycle", and the trap repeats "a full cycle has 2p pulses and 2p commutations". A full cycle has 2p pulses and every pulse has two edges (turn-on and turn-off), so the output changes level 4p times per cycle. The number 2p is the pulse count, not the edge count.
fix: Each pulse has two edges, so p pulses per half cycle give 2p pulses and 4p switching transitions per cycle. More transitions mean more switching loss in the devices and more gate-drive power. In the trap write: "... a full cycle has 2p pulses and 4p switching transitions, not p pulses and 2p transitions." Prefer the word "switching transition" or "edge" to "commutation".

problem: The lead says "One notch gives single-pulse modulation" and Q1 says "One zero-voltage notch per half cycle", but Section 1 describes the positive half cycle as +Vdc for 2d centred at 90° and zero for the rest - that is two zero intervals inside the half cycle, or equivalently one zero notch of width π−2d straddling each zero crossing. Students will not be able to reconcile the two statements.
fix: Say: single-pulse modulation gives one pulse of width 2d per half cycle, and the zero-voltage notches (width π−2d) sit on either side of each zero crossing. Multiple-pulse modulation gives p equal pulses per half cycle, each of width 2d.

problem: "the fundamental is fixed at 4Vdc/π" states a peak value without saying so; the rest of the chapter and the figure use "fundamental peak". A student may take 4Vdc/π as an rms figure.
fix: "...so the fundamental peak is fixed at 4Vdc/π, that is 1.273Vdc."
